_comment: Scripted multi-turn conversations for the DAWN request-layout A/B. Each stresses a place where moving the per-turn context block (time + retrieval) out of the system prompt could change behavior: follow-ups after tool use, memory recall and citation, [system_time] awareness, long tool loops, and back-references across turns. expect_tools: every listed tool must be called during that turn. rubric: what the judge checks (pass/fail). needs_date: the judge is given the turn's wall-clock date/time. expect_citation: a memory-recall turn, counted in cite-rate. expect_answer: regexes that must all match the answer (case-insensitive), a deterministic ground-truth check graded without the judge. opt_in: the scenario runs only when named in --only.

scenarios.why: Cross-turn continuity after tool-use turns (the exact turn shape that 400s on enforced accounts).

turns.text: Use the calculator: what is 17.5% of 2,340?
turns.rubric: States 409.5.

turns.text: Now use the calculator to add that to 1,200 and divide the result by 3.
Which of those two results is bigger, and by how much?
turns.rubric: Says 536.5 is bigger than 409.5 by 127.

scenarios.why: Retrieval injected as per-turn context; answers must use it and cite it.

turns.text: What's my dog's name, and what breed is he?
turns.rubric: Answers Biscuit, a beagle.

turns.text: I'm booking a flight to go see my sister. Which city am I flying to, and what seat should I pick?
turns.rubric: Says Denver and recommends an aisle seat (the user's stated preference).

turns.text: Suggest a type of restaurant for our anniversary dinner that's safe for me. When is the anniversary again?
turns.rubric: Gives June 14 as the anniversary and suggests something that avoids shellfish (flags or avoids the shellfish allergy; Thai is a plus but not required).

scenarios.why: [system_time] lives in the per-turn block; after a tool turn the model must still read the current time correctly.

turns.text: Quick one, use the calculator: what's 12 times 12?
turns.rubric: States 144.

turns.text: What day of the week is it today, and what's the date?
turns.rubric: Gives the correct current weekday and date (see the provided wall-clock time).

turns.text: How many days from today until December 25 this year?
turns.rubric: Gives the correct number of days from the provided current date to December 25 of the same year (off-by-one tolerated only if the answer states whether today is counted).

scenarios.why: Several tool iterations inside one turn, then a follow-up that depends on them (intra-turn cache span + thinking replay).

turns.text: Compute each of these separately with the calculator: 3 to the 7th power, 2 to the 15th power, and 17 times 23 times 29. Then give me the sum of all three.
turns.rubric: Gives 2187, 32768 and 11339, and the sum 46294.

turns.text: Divide that sum by the second result, to three decimal places.

scenarios.why: A tool call whose argument comes from injected memory, then a follow-up combining the tool result with more memory.

turns.text: What's the weather like today where my sister lives?
turns.rubric: Identifies Denver and reports current Denver weather from the tool result.

turns.text: Would that be decent weather for me to take Biscuit on a long walk if I visited?
turns.rubric: Gives a yes/no-style judgment grounded in the Denver weather just reported; correctly treats Biscuit as the user's dog; bonus if it accounts for the user disliking cold, windy weather.

scenarios.why: A longer pure-chat chain with back-references; exercises cross-turn history reuse with no retrieval dependence.

turns.text: For this chat only (don't save it to memory): the code number is 4471. Just acknowledge.
turns.rubric: Acknowledges briefly without saving to memory.

turns.text: What's that number times 3?
turns.rubric: States 13413.

turns.text: And what was the original number I gave you?
turns.rubric: States 4471.

turns.text: Summarize this whole conversation in one sentence.
turns.rubric: One sentence that mentions the number 4471 and the multiplication by 3 (13413).

scenarios.why: Questions answered by an uploaded (global) document: the relevant-document side of focus-injection calibration, and a document-retrieval regression check.

turns.text: According to the DAWN memory system design doc, why does DAWN extract memories in a batch after the session instead of in real time?
turns.rubric: Explains the batch/'sleep' choice as the doc does: extraction happens at session end rather than during the conversation so chat latency isn't affected (and it sees the whole conversation).

turns.text: In that design, do the local mic and DAP interfaces store memories by default?
turns.rubric: Says no: by default they run as guest sessions that do not store memories (users can optionally map them to an authenticated user).

turns.text: What's the default session inactivity timeout it gives for ending a memory session?
turns.rubric: Says 15 minutes (session_timeout_minutes = 15).

scenarios.why: One topic over 12 turns with the same remembered facts relevant early, mid and late, and a model switch at turn 10. Measures what retained context costs per turn and whether the answers still use a fact shown many turns back (the incremental-context change sends an item once, not every turn).

turns.text: I'm thinking about visiting my sister next month. Remind me where she lives and what she does.
turns.rubric: Says the sister (Priya) lives in Denver, Colorado, and works as a veterinarian.

turns.text: Roughly how long is a nonstop flight from Chicago to Denver?
turns.rubric: Gives a plausible nonstop duration of about 2.5 hours (anything from about 2 to 3 hours is fine).

turns.text: When I book that flight, what kind of seat should I pick for myself?
turns.rubric: Recommends an aisle seat because the user prefers aisle seats.

turns.text: Use the calculator: the fare is $289 each way and a checked bag is $35 each way. What's the round-trip total?
What's the weather in Denver right now?
turns.rubric: Reports current Denver conditions grounded in a weather lookup; no invented specifics beyond the tool's data.

turns.text: Given what you know about me, what should I pack for that, and is there anything about Denver weather I'd want to watch out for?
turns.rubric: Packing advice ties to the user's dislike of cold, windy weather (e.g. a wind layer, warm layers); mentions wind or cold as something the user specifically dislikes.

turns.text: Suggest a kind of restaurant for dinner with my sister one night.
turns.rubric: Suggests Thai food (the user's favorite cuisine) and flags avoiding shellfish because of the user's allergy.

turns.text: Actually, could I drive instead and bring my dog? What would I be driving, and is that car a good fit for the trip?
turns.rubric: Names the dog Biscuit (a beagle) and the user's blue 2019 Subaru Outback, and says it suits a long drive with a dog.

turns.text: I don't want to lose ground on my training while I'm there. What should I plan for?
turns.rubric: Ties the advice to the user's half-marathon training (e.g. keep long runs, adjust for Denver's altitude).

turns.text: Give me a three-bullet recap of the plan so far.
turns.rubric: Three bullets consistent with the conversation: visiting Priya in Denver, travel (flight with an aisle seat or driving the Subaru with Biscuit), and at least one of: Thai dinner without shellfish, packing for cold/wind, keeping up half-marathon training.

turns.text: Remind me what my sister does for work; I want to bring her a useful gift.
turns.rubric: Says she is a veterinarian and suggests a gift that fits that work.

turns.text: If she wants to take us on a windy hike and then cook seafood for dinner, what should I tell her?
turns.rubric: Mentions both: the user dislikes cold, windy weather, and the user is allergic to shellfish (so seafood dinners need to avoid shellfish).

scenarios.why: A tool result too big for the model's share of the context is sent as a view (head and tail) with a handle; the answer sits in the omitted middle, so the model must read more of the stored result (result_read) or fail honestly. The page is a pinned Wikipedia revision, so the ground truth never changes. Needs web access. url_fetch keeps up to 24,000 characters, so the view only fires on a model whose window gives a smaller share (about 200K tokens or less, e.g. claude:claude-sonnet-4-5); on a 1M-window model the whole page fits and this is a plain tool question.

turns.text: Fetch https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Apollo_11&oldid=1371120273 with url_fetch. From the fetched page text only: how many people does it say attended Kennedy's September 1962 speech at Rice University's football stadium, and which citation numbers follow that sentence? Answer from the page, not from memory.
turns.rubric: Says about 40,000 people and citations 23 and 24, taken from the fetched page (or says honestly that it couldn't find it in the page).
